references.why: Segond reads « si tu le visites la nuit » (conditional, the heart visited); the whole address is built on the KJV's completed personal visit « Thou hast visited me in the night », so it is rendered directly.
KJV Ps 8:4 = Segond 8:5. First half is Segond verbatim; Segond's second half « pour que tu prennes garde à lui » loses KJV « visitest », the theme of the address.
Spurgeon blends Zech 12:10 (Segond « vers moi, celui qu’ils ont percé ») with John 19:37, re-personing to « Him »; Segond's words kept where they fit.

Segond « Il en donne autant à ses bien-aimés pendant leur sommeil » has a different sense; Spurgeon's point (He gives them something better than sleep) depends on the KJV « He giveth his beloved sleep ».
KJV Ps 34:8 = Segond 34:9. Segond « Sentez et voyez » now reads as 'smell'; the honey/tasting argument needs « goûter ».
Segond « Il regarde par le treillis » loses KJV « showing himself », which is the point (the Lord's manifestations).
Re-personed paraphrase (our heart, present tense) of Segond « la paix de Dieu ... gardera vos cœurs et vos pensées en Jésus-Christ ».
Spurgeon blends Ps 121:6 with Rev 7:16 ("nor any heat") and re-persons it to "us"; rendered on Segond's vocabulary (frapper, ni aucune chaleur).

Segond reads « J’ai désiré m’asseoir à son ombre », losing KJV "I sat down ... with great delight" on which the whole second head ("a place of sitting down", "delight") is built; kept Segond's second line.
Repeated KJV "I sat down under His shadow" (and in the hymn); Segond's « J’ai désiré m’asseoir » would break the argument.
Allusion to "the good old way ... rest unto your souls", re-personed to "our souls".
Re-personed ("our heart") inside a composed prayer; Segond has « Mon cœur est affermi ».
KJV "thou hast been our dwelling place"; Segond has « refuge », and the address turns on dwelling; re-tensed inside a composed prayer.
Allusion "come boldly unto Him"; Segond word « avec assurance » applied to Christ.
Re-personed and re-tensed from Segond « la joie de l’Éternel sera votre force ».

KJV 63:7 = Segond 63:8. Segond « tu es mon secours » is present tense, but Spurgeon's point ("he sings rather of memories"; "Thou hast been my help" as the highest note) depends on the KJV past tense.
Same past-tense KJV wording the argument rests on.
Segond « Il m’a couvert de l’ombre de sa main » adapted to describe workers (plural participle).

Segond 2:3a « J’ai désiré m’asseoir à son ombre » loses the KJV « I sat down under His shadow with great delight » on which the whole address is built (sitting down, great delight); first clause rendered from the KJV, second clause is Segond verbatim.
KJV image (sat down, with great delight) kept; Segond reads « J’ai désiré m’asseoir à son ombre ».
Spurgeon's own resolution-form paraphrase of the KJV « I sat down under his shadow ».
Allusion re-personed to the first person (Segond: « qu’on rejettera votre nom comme infâme »).
KJV 'I sat down under his shadow'; Segond 'J’ai désiré m’asseoir à son ombre' loses the act of sitting down on which the whole address turns (and 'she did not climb, she sat').
Re-personed into 'we' and recast as a statement (Segond's wording kept for the phrases).
Re-personed into 'we'; Segond's wording kept otherwise.
KJV 'the king sitteth at his table'; Segond 'le roi est dans son entourage' loses the table the argument (the King sits and eats, so do we) depends on.
Re-personed allusion.
Re-personed allusion.
Spurgeon quotes KJV in the singular ('O friend') and his point is 'drink abundantly' (you cannot have too much); Segond 'Mangez, amis, buvez, enivrez-vous d’amour!' differs in number and image.
Paraphrase ('the motto of that banneret was love').

Segond's « Avant que le jour se rafraîchisse » loses the daybreak image the address turns on (« until the day break » = no day till Christ appears), and « qui nous séparent » loses the proper name Bether, which Spurgeon keeps (« ces montagnes de Béther »).
Segond: « Reviens!… sois semblable, mon bien-aimé »; the vocative is re-ordered to follow KJV « Turn, my Beloved ».
Spurgeon's own rendering « mountains of division » (the margin reading of Bether); the closing words follow Segond, the rest is re-joined to his KJV wording.
Segond « N’abandonnez donc pas votre assurance »; « donc » dropped since the sentence already carries it.
Segond renders the verse as a wish (« Que sa main gauche soit… »); Spurgeon quotes it (KJV) as a present reality she had just sung.
Blend of Ephesians 2:4, 2:5 and 2:1 as Spurgeon quotes it; « grand amour dont il nous a aimés » and « morts par nos offenses » are Segond.
Segond « Elles ne comptent pas sur l’homme, Elles ne dépendent pas des enfants des hommes », put in the singular to fit Spurgeon's « the dew ».
Re-personed (« pour vous ») as Spurgeon applies it to the hearer.
Segond « Il regarde par la fenêtre »; Spurgeon applies it to « these windows » (the bread and wine).

Segond renders the verse « Je ne sais, mais mon désir m’a rendue semblable Aux chars de mon noble peuple », losing the KJV proper name Amminadib and « or ever I was aware »; rendered from Spurgeon's KJV.
Re-personed (« nous ») and blended with « the King » of Song 1:4; « banqueting-house » kept as « maison du festin » (Segond: « maison du vin »).
Re-personed: Segond reads « os de mes os et chair de ma chair »; Spurgeon applies it in the third person to the Church.
Segond reads « qu’il nous a accordée en son bien-aimé », losing KJV « accepted in the Beloved », the word Spurgeon’s point (a positive righteousness conferred) turns on.
Segond renders « Que tu es belle, mon amie, que tu es belle! », dropping the KJV « Behold » that Spurgeon’s argument explicitly builds on (« He puts a “behold” before it »).
Same as above: KJV « Behold » kept because the argument depends on it.
Re-personed (« we ») from Segond « C’est le soleil qui m’a brûlée ».
Paraphrase, not a quotation: KJV « he loved them unto the end », Segond « mit le comble à son amour ».
Segond reads « Je veux faire ta volonté », losing KJV « I delight to do thy will », which Spurgeon quotes to prove « how Christ did delight » in redemption.
Wisdom's first-person line re-personed to the third person as Spurgeon quotes it; Segond wording otherwise kept (« trouvant mon bonheur parmi les fils de l’homme »).
Segond reads « les jours qui m’étaient destinés »; Spurgeon's point (Christ's members, the elect, written in his book) rests on the KJV word « members ».

Allusion following the KJV (« He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied »), set in the past tense by Spurgeon; Segond's « il rassasiera ses regards » does not carry the same sense.
Allusion to KJV Acts 3:19 (Segond 3:20); Segond says « de la part du Seigneur », kept KJV « from the presence of the Lord »; « des temps de rafraîchissement » is Segond's wording.
Blended paraphrase (Matthew 26:22 « Est-ce moi, Seigneur? » with the betrayal of John 13), not a single verse.
Segond renders the line as a wish (« Que sa main gauche soit sous ma tête, Et que sa droite m’embrasse! »); Spurgeon sings it as a present, possessed assurance (KJV indicative).

Segond ('toute sa personne est pleine de charme') loses 'altogether' and 'lovely' = worthy of love, on which the whole address turns (Part I contrasts 'not beautiful, nor admirable, but lovely'); rendered 'tout aimable' consistently throughout (heading and body).
Unquoted allusion, re-cast as a participle clause.
Unquoted paraphrase of the verse's imagery; Segond vocabulary kept (chrysolithes for KJV beryl) but recast in Spurgeon's sentence.
Unquoted paraphrase; Segond vocabulary, 'blanc' dropped as Spurgeon has only 'marble'.
KJV comparative 'marred more than any man' is Spurgeon's point; Segond phrases it differently ('Tant son visage était défiguré').
KJV 'accepted in the Beloved' carries the argument (made lovely to the Father); Segond reads 'sa grâce qu’il nous a accordée en son bien-aimé'.
Unquoted allusion, re-personed from Segond's 'en qui j’ai mis toute mon affection'.
Segond wording put into the future tense to fit Spurgeon's sentence.
Blend of 1 John 3:2 with Psalm 17:15 ('satisfied'), unquoted.
Segond's « toute sa personne est pleine de charme » loses 'altogether lovely', on which the address turns
Unquoted allusion to KJV Ps 7:11 (Segond 7:12) 'God is angry with the wicked every day'; Segond reads 'Dieu s’irrite en tout temps' without 'the wicked', so Spurgeon's wording is rendered.
Unquoted allusion, re-personed into Spurgeon's sentence.
Imperative 'walk in the light'; Segond 1 John 1:7 has 'si nous marchons dans la lumière' (first person plural).
Allusion re-personed to the third person (Segond: « trouvant mes délices parmi les fils de l’homme »).
Loose allusion: Spurgeon says « the servant of the Lord » where Zechariah has « as the angel of the LORD » (Segond: « comme l’ange de l’Éternel »); translated as Spurgeon wrote it.
Hymn paraphrase (Irons) built on KJV « Stay me with flagons »; Segond has « gâteaux de raisins », which loses the wine image the stanza depends on.
Hymn paraphrase (Irons) of « comfort me with apples », re-personed.
Spurgeon turns the verse into an exhortation; Segond: « vos entrailles se sont rétrécies ».
Spurgeon’s blended echo of Ps 32:11 (‘be glad in the Lord’) addressed to his own soul; re-personed, Segond’s wording (‘Justes, réjouissez-vous en l’Éternel’) does not fit.
KJV ‘thy thoughts unto me are precious’; Segond reads ‘me semblent impénétrables’, losing the word ‘precious’ the prayer turns on.
Paraphrase of KJV Ps 30:7 (Segond 30:8), re-personed from first to second person.
KJV ‘refuge of lies’ (Isa 28:15, 17); Segond’s ‘le mensonge pour abri’ / ‘le refuge de la fausseté’ does not fit the plural phrase.
Paraphrase of John 16:14 recast in the third person (‘the things of Christ’) with ‘reveal’.
Re-personed allusion (ma chair → sa chair) in an infinitive construction.
Re-personed from ‘je souperai avec lui, et lui avec moi’.
Spurgeon re-persons the verse ("Our Well-beloved hath a vineyard"); rendered in the present with « Notre ».
Allusion re-personed ("He bought us with a price"); Segond's « rachetés à un grand prix » kept inside.

Re-personed KJV wording ("the lines have fallen unto us in pleasant places; yea, we have a goodly heritage"); Segond drops the 'lines/pleasant places' image, so rendered from the KJV with Segond's vocabulary.
Allusion re-personed in the past tense ("you served the Lord with gladness").
Allusion; Spurgeon's image is the KJV 'rose', Segond has « narcisse ».
KJV phrase 'good hope through grace'; Segond reads « une bonne espérance » given « par sa grâce ».

Segond has the present « je te rachète »; the whole address turns on the KJV perfect 'I have redeemed thee' (a redemption already accomplished: 'Redemption is a fact accomplished… This is done'), so the perfect is kept. Used as the heading text and as the refrain throughout.
Isaiah 43:1 re-cast in the perfect ('I have redeemed thee. I have called thee'); Segond has « je te rachète, Je t’appelle ».
Unquoted allusion resting on the KJV reading 'and not we ourselves'; Segond reads « et nous lui appartenons », which loses the point.
KJV 'it behoved Christ to suffer'; Segond 24:46 reads « il est écrit que le Christ souffrirait », so the 'it behoved' sense is rendered (wording modelled on Segond Luke 24:26).
Re-personed ('our head'); Segond « votre tête ».
Re-personed ('He careth for us'); Segond « lui-même prend soin de vous ».
Unquoted paraphrase ('He carrieth the lambs in His bosom'); Segond « Il prendra les agneaux dans ses bras, Et les portera dans son sein ».
Unquoted allusion in the present tense ('The stars in their courses fight'); Segond « De leurs sentiers les étoiles combattirent ».
Unquoted paraphrase in the third person; Segond « à cause de ton alliance scellée par le sang, Je retirerai tes captifs ».
KJV 'O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength' (a triumph accomplished); Segond reads « Mon âme, foule aux pieds les héros! » (imperative, different object), which loses the sense Spurgeon uses.

Segond reads « mon serviteur prospérera; Il montera, il s’élèvera »; Spurgeon expounds the KJV 'deal prudently' and the distinction between 'exalted' (his state) and 'extolled' (the praise rendered him), which Segond's wording does not carry. Only the final clause « il s’élèvera bien haut » is Segond's.

Segond has « un sujet d’effroi » and « Tant son aspect différait de celui des fils de l’homme »; the whole address is built on KJV 'astonied' (astonishment, the chapter title) and on 'marred more than any man … more than the sons of men'.

Segond reads « il sera pour beaucoup de peuples un sujet de joie »; Spurgeon expounds the KJV 'sprinkle' at length (sprinkling of blood, Heb 9-10) and mentions Segond's reading only as an alternative ('exult with joy, for so some read').
Re-personed into a prayer addressed to Christ.
Spurgeon paraphrases in the first person plural and present tense ('doth … purge our conscience'); Segond's « purifiera-t-il votre conscience … afin que vous serviez » re-personed.
KJV Isaiah 9:7 = Segond 9:6; Segond's wording (« Donner à l’empire de l’accroissement, Et une paix sans fin ») is an infinitive clause continuing 9:5 and cannot stand alone as the quoted sentence.
Segond reads « qu’il nous a accordée en son bien-aimé »; Spurgeon’s point rests on the KJV word “accepted”, applied to the Church (re-personed).
Cited in Spurgeon’s list for “thy brother”, but Segond reads « tes frères »; the list citation is loose, not wrong.
Re-personed from Segond « os de mes os et chair de ma chair ».
Paraphrase of the statue description, not a quotation.
Segond addresses the worms in the plural (« Vous êtes ma mère et ma sœur »); Spurgeon’s singular “the worm … Thou art my sister” kept.
Re-personed from Segond « je hais la répudiation » (KJV “He hateth putting away”).
Allusion re-personed from Segond « j’ai mis devant toi une porte ouverte ».
Allusion in present tense; Segond « chaque porte était d’une seule perle ».
Allusion blended; Segond « l’âme de Jonathan fut attachée à l’âme de David, et Jonathan l’aima comme son âme ».
Spurgeon's condensed form of the verse (omits 'all ye that labour and are heavy laden'); both halves are Segond's words.
Re-personed allusion ('come and learn of Jesus, and thou shalt find rest') addressed to the soul in the singular, built on Segond's 'recevez mes instructions … vous trouverez du repos'.
KJV 'Rest in the LORD'; Segond's 'Garde le silence devant l’Éternel' loses the word 'rest' the whole address turns on. Second half is Segond's.
KJV 'and this is the refreshing'; Segond has 'Voici le lieu du repos', losing the word 'refreshing' that Spurgeon's point (rest refreshes) rests on. First half follows Segond.
Segond’s « les cantiques » loses the singular ‘an hymn’ the address turns on
Segond’s « les cantiques » loses the singular ‘an hymn’ the address turns on
Paraphrased into the third person (Christ's own words re-personed).
Woven into narrative in the third person; Segond (and the psalm) address God as « tu ».
Past-historic narrative form of Segond's « Les flots les ont couverts », woven into Spurgeon's sentence.
KJV image (Rahab cut, the dragon wounded); Segond renders Rahab as « l’Égypte » and the dragon as « le monstre », losing the names Spurgeon sings of.
Spurgeon blends Exodus 14:8 (« la main levée ») with Deuteronomy 26:8 (« à bras étendu »).
Blend of Exodus 15:5 (« Les flots les ont couverts ») and Exodus 14:28 (« il n’en échappa pas un seul »), in Spurgeon's present-perfect form.
Re-personed from Segond's « tu as été immolé, et tu as racheté pour Dieu par ton sang ».
Recast as a present participle clause (« leading captivity captive, ascending up on high »); Segond: « Étant monté en haut, il a emmené des captifs ».
Recast in the past tense with « troupeau » (Spurgeon's « flock »); Segond: « Le bon berger donne sa vie pour ses brebis ».
Spurgeon blends John 6:50-51 (bread come down from heaven, whoever eats) with John 6:35 (shall never hunger); rendered as one phrase, Segond wording used where it carries the same words.
Allusion adapted to Christ's love (past tense, 'his love'); Segond's 'Les grandes eaux ne peuvent éteindre l’amour' reshaped to fit the sentence.
KJV 'sung an hymn' (singular) is the address's theme; Segond has the plural 'Après avoir chanté les cantiques'.
Re-personed and put in the past from Segond 'Mon âme est triste jusqu’à la mort'.
Re-personed (our/has rejoiced) from Segond 'mon esprit se réjouit en Dieu, mon Sauveur'.
Re-personed (their) from Segond 'par vos offenses et par vos péchés'.
Spurgeon's argument is that even the dumb shall SING; Segond's 'la langue du muet éclatera de joie' loses the verb 'sing' (KJV 'the tongue of the dumb sing').
Spurgeon counts David's repeated 'I will sing'; Segond's 'Je chanterai, je célébrerai l’Éternel' drops the repetition his point rests on.
Re-personed (you) from Segond 'qui m’a aimé et qui s’est livré lui-même pour moi'.
Unmarked allusion (KJV 'continued with me in my temptations'), re-personed into Spurgeon's narration.
Allusion to KJV 'he giveth his beloved sleep'; Segond's wording ('Il en donne autant à ses bien-aimés pendant leur sommeil') does not carry the image Spurgeon uses.
Re-personed allusion applied to the sailors ('reels to and fro, and staggers like a drunken man, and is at his wits' end').
Re-personed from God's word to Abram ('I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward').
Spurgeon's phrase 'perfect peace' (KJV) carries his point; Segond renders the Hebrew doubling as 'la paix, la paix'.
Allusion re-tensed ("where there is no more sea"); Segond has the past tense.
Re-personed allusion ('the works which Jesus did shall we do also').
Allusion to KJV 'he giveth his beloved sleep'; Segond's wording loses the image.
KJV 'What is the chaff to the wheat?' is a contrast of worth that Spurgeon applies to the crowd; Segond ('Pourquoi mêler la paille au froment?') asks about mixing, which loses the point.
Re-personed paraphrase (first person, past tense) of the woman's words, blended with Matthew 9:20 'le bord de son vêtement'.
Allusive title woven into Spurgeon's sentence; Segond's 'Celui qui juge toute la terre' does not fit the noun phrase.
Allusion blending Romans 6:4 and Colossians 2:12, re-personed and negated; follows Segond's vocabulary (ensevelis ... par le baptême, nouveauté de vie).
Re-personed into Christ's mouth (KJV 'thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands'); Segond's 'Tu languirais après l’ouvrage de tes mains' cannot be carried into first person verbatim.
Spurgeon's argument turns on the KJV words 'unworthily' (adverb) and 'damnation'; Segond 11:29 has neither ('sans discerner le corps du Seigneur ... un jugement'), so the KJV wording is rendered.
Repetition of the KJV wording his adjective/adverb argument depends on; not in Segond 11:29.
Segond's wording re-personed to the hearer (« son bon sens » → « votre bon sens »).
Allusion applied to one sinner (singular « blanc »; Segond has « blancs »); the scarlet-dye image is Spurgeon's own development.
Paraphrase (also Psalm 113:7) reordered into Spurgeon's sentence; Segond: « Du fumier il relève l’indigent ».
Segond's « Pour les faire asseoir avec les grands » re-personed to « nous ».
Spurgeon's point rests on the KJV proper name Ammi-nadib; Segond renders it « mon noble peuple », losing the image. Re-personed to the hearer.
Spurgeon's third-person adaptation of « Quelqu’un m’a touché ».
Segond « Ce qu’il a fait à mon âme » re-personed to the hearer, with « le Seigneur » as in Spurgeon.
Re-personed from 'my yoke' to 'his yoke'; otherwise Segond's wording.
Spurgeon's point turns on the KJV reading ('must show himself friendly'); Segond renders the verse quite differently ('les a pour son malheur').
Re-personed allusion ('I will sup with him, and he with me').
Allusion to 'eat bread in the kingdom of God', re-personed; Segond has 'prendra son repas'.
Paraphrase, re-personed ('that which I have committed unto him' -> 'we').
Allusion inside Spurgeon's imagined speech of Christ, adapted.
Allusion re-personed inside Spurgeon's imagined speech of Christ.
Paraphrased exhortation ('see that ye love each other with a pure heart fervently'), blended with KJV's 'pure heart'.
Paraphrased allusion, re-personed.
Allusion to 'newness of life'; Segond has 'nouveauté de vie'.
Spurgeon quotes the KJV 'One is your Master, even Christ'; Segond 23:8 has no 'le Christ' (textual variant), so Segond's wording is kept with 'le Christ' added from the KJV.
Indirect paraphrase in Spurgeon's own sentence, not a quotation.
Allusion re-worded by Spurgeon ('his meat and his drink … the will of the heavenly Father'), not a quotation.
Loose allusion (KJV-style 'the Lord's arm is not shortened'); Segond says 'la main de l’Éternel n’est pas trop courte', so Spurgeon's image is rendered directly.
Allusion re-personed into the first person future ('we shall subdue kingdoms yet'); Segond: 'vainquirent des royaumes'.
Re-personed to the hearers (vous); Segond: 'crois seulement'.
Segond's « parfait en Christ » put in the plural to agree with « vous »; KJV 'perfect in Christ Jesus'.
Re-personed allusion; keeps KJV 'covered' image (Segond: « pardonné »).
Spurgeon's abridged form of the verse; Segond's full wording adds « par lui … dont vous ne pouviez être justifiés par la loi ».
KJV 'Whence is this to me?' used as the believer's own cry; adapted from Segond « Comment m’est-il accordé ».
Spurgeon's argument is imputed righteousness (KJV 'righteousness of saints'); Segond's « œuvres justes des saints » would shift the doctrine.
Allusion blending Segond's 'liens de la mort' and 'il n’était pas possible qu’il fût retenu par elle' into one clause.
KJV 'waits to be gracious'; Segond has 'désire vous faire grâce', which loses the waiting image Spurgeon uses.
Re-personed blend of 12:8 ('de l’éloigner de moi') and 12:7 ('écharde dans la chair') as the hearer's own words.
Re-personed allusion (Segond: 'L’Éternel est mon berger').
Allusion to KJV 'valley of the shadow of death' in Spurgeon's phrasing.
Re-personed paraphrase (Segond: 'Je ne te délaisserai point, et je ne t’abandonnerai point').
Plural of Segond's 'sage à salut' to fit the sentence.
Allusion to KJV 'eat up my people as they eat bread'; Segond's wording ('le prennent pour nourriture') does not fit the image.
Spurgeon's interpretive expansion of the verse.
Re-personed to the singular in the hearer's prayer.
Spurgeon's expansion with 'now'.
Allusion re-cast as a past statement about Jesus (Segond wording kept where possible).
Blend of John 20:25 and 20:27, re-personed to 'we'.
Allusion re-cast around Christ as bridegroom (Segond: 'La myrrhe, l’aloès et la casse parfument tous tes vêtements').
Segond's wording (which keeps the 'mountains of separation' image) with its verse-line capitals and comma adjusted, blended into Spurgeon's prayer.
KJV 'the word upon which thou hast caused me to hope'; Segond has 'ta promesse … Puisque tu m’as donné l’espérance' — recast.
Spurgeon quotes the Revised Version ('a communion') and comments on 'a' vs 'the'; Segond's 'la communion' would erase his point.
Revised Version margin reading 'the loaf'; his argument rests on 'loaf' (unity), rendered « miche » since Segond's « pain » cannot carry the contrast.
Revised Version wording ('one loaf, one body'), which Spurgeon expounds; Segond's structure differs.
Allusive paraphrase of the KJV ('manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world'), recast as a statement.
Allusion to KJV 'windows of agates, gates of carbuncles'; Segond reads 'créneaux de rubis', losing the windows/gates image Spurgeon uses.
Spurgeon's adaptation ('given this communion'); Segond's feminine pronouns (the light/Word) also re-personed to Christ.
KJV 'spake often'; the word 'often' (absent in Segond) carries his contrast 'more often speak one against another'.
Re-personed from the imperative to 'we', following Segond's wording.
Re-personed to 'you' (plural), following Segond's wording.
Segond's pronouns are feminine (referring to the light/Word); re-personed to Christ ('l’ont reçu', 'il a donné') as Spurgeon applies it.
Spurgeon quotes the KJV marginal reading (“to the tree”) to make his point; Segond reads « sur le bois », so « jusque sur le bois » is rendered from his wording.
KJV joins “slain” to “from the foundation of the world”; Segond attaches that phrase to the names written in the book of life, so Spurgeon’s phrase is rendered from the KJV.
Unquoted allusion, re-personed (“He hath cast all our iniquities”) and blended with Isaiah 38:17; Segond’s « Tu jetteras au fond de la mer tous leurs péchés » differs in person and tense.
Unquoted allusion, re-personed from Hezekiah’s « tu as jeté derrière toi tous mes péchés ».
Unquoted allusion to the dove, re-personed (« son pied » → « notre pied »).

Segond has no 'Amen' and reads 'les clefs de la mort et du séjour des morts' (reversed order, 'séjour des morts'); Spurgeon expounds 'the keys of hell' (the devil's house, the lion caged) and then 'and of death' as two successive clauses, so the KJV order and 'hell' are kept.
Spurgeon's exposition turns on KJV 'hell' (the devil's own house whose keys hang at Christ's girdle); Segond's 'séjour des morts' would lose it.
Final clause of the KJV order 'the keys of hell and of death'; Segond reverses the order.
Spurgeon's summary of 'this do in remembrance of me' as a command, not Segond's wording.
Re-personed (applied to the vain man) from Segond's 'nous soyons par nous-mêmes capables de concevoir quelque chose comme venant de nous-mêmes'.
KJV 'in all their affliction he was afflicted'; Segond follows the other Hebrew reading ('ils n'ont pas été sans secours'), which loses the point of Christ's sympathy.
KJV image 'a brother is born for adversity'; Segond ('dans le malheur il se montre un frère') does not fit the sentence as a title of Christ.
Re-personed (first person plural) from Segond's 'os de mes os et chair de ma chair'.
KJV Micah 5:7 (Segond 5:6) re-personed into Christ's first-person speech.
KJV 'The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me'; Segond ('agira en ma faveur') lacks the 'perfecting' Spurgeon uses; also re-personed.
Echo of KJV 'until the day break'; Segond reads 'Avant que le jour se rafraîchisse'.
